findings.evidence: _STEMS lacks apikey and other *key stems; 'apikey' matches only as a whole word in _SENSITIVE_WORDS. The short-code rule needs an all-digit value. field_is_sensitive({'type':'text','name':N,'value':'Zx9-kq_7Lm'}) is False for stripeapikey, openaiapikey, myapikey, userapikey, xapikey, accessKey, accesskey, signingkey, sessionkey, encryptionkey and masterkey, and for recovery_code/backup_code (label 'Recovery code') with value '7f3a9-2c1d8'. Real Chromium (run_snapshot.cjs) on a page with those inputs returned sensitive:false with the values. AssistCommands assist_ask (FakeAdapter fed the Chromium snapshot, FakeClient) put all four values (Zq81LmXv0PaT, Wk22HnRt9QbU, 7f3a9-2c1d8, Pp55TrEw3ZaQ) into the Brain request body. 'my', 'user', 'client' and 'access' are in the R3 test's own PREFIXES list, but 'apikey' is not among its STEMS. A0_QUALIFICATION again claims 'MET in both layers after the R3 repair'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add apikey and (api|access|auth|private|secret|signing|encryption|master|session|client|hmac)key stems to _STEMS/STEMS. Treat recovery/backup code fields as sensitive whatever the value. Add these to the generated corpus and the Chromium parity test, and correct the A0_QUALIFICATION claim.
findings.title: Redaction still misses run-together API-key names and alphanumeric 2FA recovery codes in both Python and the in-page JS (R3-01 token/secret class not closed); values reach the Brain request

findings.evidence: _NUMBER captures only %/percent/million/billion/thousand units. verify('The company raised $5bn in new funding from investors this year [1].', ['The company raised $5m in new funding from investors this year.']) -> KEPT. Also KEPT: $5k->$5M, '2 lakh'->'2 crore', 'Rs.500 crore'->'Rs.500 trillion', '5 km'->'5 miles'. EV.evaluate on two sources '$5m' vs '$5bn' -> 0 conflicts; '2 lakh' vs '2 crore' -> 0 conflicts ('Rs.500' vs 'Rs.900' -> 1). The surface states 'citations checked against the sources (wording, numbers, negation)'. W1-AC10/AC11.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise attached magnitude tokens (k, m, mn, bn, b, M, trillion, lakh, crore, and their plurals/abbreviations) into the number key, and treat a scale word next to a number as part of it. Add regression cases for $5m/$5bn, lakh/crore and trillion.
findings.title: Citation verifier and conflict detector ignore magnitude suffixes (m/bn/k/M, lakh/crore, trillion), so a claim with a different magnitude survives verify

findings.evidence: The deadline and the cancel flag are checked only between body chunks. The httpx read timeout applies per socket read. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R4/ssrf/p4_sockets.py: a real local server drips header bytes every 0.3 s; SafeFetcher(read_timeout=1.0, total_timeout=2.0) with cancel at 1.0 s returned UNREACHABLE after 67.3 s (re-run by me). A chunk-extension drip returned CANCELLED only after 12.1 s with total_timeout 2.0. A server that drips under the 10 s default read timeout holds the fetch with no bound, and WebResearch stays busy (RESEARCH_IN_PROGRESS). W1-AC4 (total timeout) and W1-AC13 (cooperative cancellation) are unmet against a hostile page.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce a wall-clock deadline on the whole request, e.g. a watchdog timer that closes the response/transport at min(deadline, cancel), or per-read timeouts recomputed from the remaining budget. Add a slow-header regression test with a real socket.
findings.title: SafeFetcher total timeout and cancellation are not enforced while response headers or chunk framing arrive; a hostile server can hold a fetch (and the single research job) far beyond the budget

findings.evidence: NP.check_address('64:ff9b:1:7f00:0:100:808:808') -> accepted (the /48 embedding is 127.0.0.1); '64:ff9b:1:a9fe:a9:fe00:808:808' -> accepted (169.254.169.254). The last 32 bits are taken as the IPv4, then the code returns early. Only exploitable on networks running a local-use NAT64 with a non-/96 prefix, with attacker-controlled DNS.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse 64:ff9b:1::/48 outright, or check every RFC 6052 embedding position.
findings.title: Local-use NAT64 64:ff9b:1::/48 decoded as /96, so addresses embedding a private IPv4 at the /48 position are accepted

findings.evidence: Probe (/tmp/uri_review_R4/a0/probe_bridge.py): grant -> ask -> revoke -> assist_ask_status returns FINISHED with the answer text. _answers is never cleared on revoke.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear _answers on revoke and on a new grant, and re-check the grant generation under the lock before storing or emitting.
findings.title: R1-05 still present: derived answers remain retrievable after Stop; a revoke that races the end of an answer still emits it

findings.evidence: With vision disabled (the default), assist_ask with use_screenshot=true -> VISION_NOT_QUALIFIED after adapter.screenshot() was called once; the same for debounced and busy. vision.build_request appends raw context_text after 'QUESTION:', so page text containing '\n\nQUESTION: ...' forges the question (03 §4 says content goes only in data blocks). Latent: no real adapter exists, and vision is off by default.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the qualified/debounce/idle checks before capture, and wrap context_text with uri_web.untrusted.data_block.
findings.title: Screenshot and DOM capture run before the vision and Brain-busy gates; vision context text is not wrapped as an untrusted data block

findings.evidence: Code reading: the cancel is gated on kind == 'oi_turn'. Orchestrator.confirm also reaches _answer_turn. make_complete uses complete_json (60 s) with no cancel token. Not executed live.

findings.title: Only oi_turn cancels Assist Brain work; oi_confirm/oi_decide and in-flight web_research Brain calls do not yield the single slot
